6. Ice and Water Density: Since the density of ice is less than the density of water at 0°C, when ice is placed on water, it displaces more water than its own weight. Therefore, the buoyancy force is greater than the weight of ice, making it float.

7. Melting Point: As we go deeper, the pressure increases. At pressures above 1 atmosphere, ice has a higher density than water. This is why diamonds are made of carbon, a solid at room temperature and pressure, but graphite, a solid at high temperature and low pressure, is denser than diamond.

8. Iceberg Example: This is why we see only a small part of an iceberg above water, as the rest of it is submerged underwater due to its density properties.

So, ice floats on water because its density is less than water at 0°C.
